patch_description: The current Kalman+Holt cascade achieves smoothness but correlation only 0.85 (Gen 13/17 reached 0.93) and lag_error is high (0.43). The recommendation points to the proven mechanism: a recency-weighted Savitzky-Golay-style local quadratic fit evaluated at the window's leading edge. A quadratic (poly_order=2) weighted least-squares fit over the window, with the time axis centered so the newest sample is t=0, analytically removes group delay: the fitted value at t=0 IS the leading-edge estimate, so lag is near zero while the polynomial fit provides strong noise suppression. The exponential recency weighting (linspace(-1.5, 0)) both suppresses noise (more weight on many averaged samples) and compensates any residual smoothing bias toward recent dynamics. On top of this, I keep a light trend-lock slope damping (EMA on the fitted slope, blended back at 35% weight) to suppress noise-induced directional reversals — this directly targets slope_changes and false_reversals without reintroducing lag into the level estimate. The 3x3 normal-equation solve per window keeps execution time well within budget (prior similar implementation ran in 0.11s with efficiency 1.00).
